name: Who bears the loss when an AI agent transacts
description: Bank and venue policies on who bears the loss when an AI agent transacts.
attribution: The Agent Economy (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/agent-loss-liability.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

rows.what_the_terms_say: Chase prohibits third-party use of login credentials and permits customer-authorized access to account data through approved APIs. If a customer gives an agent access, Chase treats the agent's actions as authorized by the customer and holds the customer responsible for errors, unintended transactions, and actions beyond the authority granted.

The upcoming agreement treats an AI agent's instructions, actions, and transactions as directly authorized by the customer without further verification. The customer uses the agent at their own risk and is responsible for monitoring it.

rows.what_the_terms_say: Citi told TechCrunch that customers who grant access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents, and TechCrunch reports the updated terms also make customers responsible if the tool leaks credentials or is hacked. Citi told USA TODAY it bars direct login and transactions by third-party agents and permits limited read-only access through certain approved providers. Citi's agreement text was not checked.
TechCrunch reported that PNC changed its terms on November 18, 2026, in its report on banks telling customers they are responsible for their agents. PNC's terms were not checked.
TechCrunch saw an email from Citizens warning customers they are responsible for what their AI assistant does. Citizens' terms were not checked.

USA TODAY reported that Bank of America is restricting AI agent access to consumer deposits and that its CEO described giving an agent your credentials as authorizing the payment. Loss allocation is not documented in the report. Bank of America's terms were not checked.
Schwab blocks unauthorized agents that try to move client money. USA TODAY reported that Schwab's own assistant, Charley, cannot execute trades.
Hunton says card transactions that use tokenized agent credentials route through network rules and the consent attached to the token, and that chargeback and liability allocation will be set there.
